title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are Grothendieck's 1986 notes on 'ateliers' (workshops), an axiomatic framework for combinatorial or 'spatial' structures. The neighbouring pages compare At_ens (a set-theoretic atelier) with At_spat (a spatial one).

Previous page. A 'rapport spatial' is a set A with a symmetric relation |o| (disjointness or orthogonality). Its biorthogonally closed subsets form a complete lattice, with smallest element A_00 and largest element A. Taking the orthogonal gives an involutive, order-reversing complementation C. One gets X ∧ CX = 0 exactly when X|o|X implies X ∈ A_00. This is the classical passage from an orthogonality space to a complete ortholattice, via the Galois connection of a symmetric relation (a Birkhoff polarity).

Applied to A = Σ, a 'spatios' (Σ, ≤, C) is a complete lattice with 0_Σ and an involutive order-reversing complement, with X|o|Y defined as X ≤ CY. Then orth(A) = {Z : Z ≤ Inf CA = C Sup A}. Hence the closed subsets correspond to principal ideals ↓ξ, and Σ is recovered from (Σ, |o|).

This page.
1. The top lines conclude that under this identification the 'rapport' generated by a part A ⊂ Σ is ξ = Sup A, and its orthogonal is Cξ.
2. A crossed-out sentence would have stated the functorial passage (A, Δ, |o|) → (Σ, ≤, C).
3. The main definition: a spatial figure in Σ is a pair (Φ, ρ) with Φ ⊂ Σ and ρ a relation on Φ such that:
   - Figspat 1: ρ is an order on Φ.
   - Figspat 2a: every X ∈ Φ is nonzero.
   - Figspat 2b: distinct elements of Φ are orthogonal (X ≤ CY).
   So a figure is a family of pairwise disjoint nonzero 'regions' carrying an abstract order. That order is not induced by ≤, since distinct members are disjoint.
4. The NB says one could be more demanding, modelling ρ on the 'rapports' structure, but this is postponed.
5. Figspat(Σ) is introduced as the set of such figures.

Next page. Elementary figures (Φ has a greatest element) form At_spat(Σ) ⊂ At_ens(Σ), with three relations:
- ⊲ is induced from At_ens.
- ≪ is defined by an increasing refinement map φ: each X ∈ Φ lies under a unique X' ∈ Φ', and φ sends greatest element to greatest element.
- |o| is strengthened to orthogonality of the top elements.

Purpose: build a 'spatial atelier' from an orthocomplemented lattice, i.e. transplant the set-theoretic atelier of finite ordered configurations into a point-free, lattice-theoretic setting.
errors: No outright error on this page. On the next page, uniqueness of X' with X ≤ X' needs X ∧ CX = 0 for X ≠ 0 (orthocomplementation, not mere involution). Grothendieck flagged exactly this condition on the previous page, so it is presumably part of the spatios axioms, but it is not restated here.
The definition of 'figure' leaves ρ completely unconstrained relative to (Σ, ≤, C). The NB acknowledges this provisional character.

ideas.what: Recovering a complete orthocomplemented lattice from its orthogonality relation via biorthogonal closure; Σ ≅ closed subsets via Sup
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / polarity Galois connection; ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets

ideas.what: Spatial figure: a family of pairwise orthogonal nonzero elements of an ortholattice equipped with an abstract order relation
ideas.modern_name: Ordered orthogonal family / labelled orthogonal decomposition (closest: orthogonal sets in quantum logic, labelled disjoint regions in mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard counterpart with the extra order; orthogonal families are standard in quantum logic

ideas.what: Embedding spatial figures into the set-theoretic atelier At_ens, with the orthogonality relation strengthened (next page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'spatios' is essentially a complete ortholattice built from an orthogonality ('rapport spatial') structure, which is exactly the framework of quantum logic and of Foulis–Randall orthogonality spaces. His 'figures' are ordered orthogonal families. This link between his 1986 search for a point-free, discrete notion of space (ateliers) and quantum-logic and mereotopological axiomatics seems unrecorded in the literature.
missed.quote: ∀ X, Y ∈ Φ, X ≠ Y ⟹ X |∘| Y (i.e. X ≤ CY)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It situates Grothendieck's late foundational 'ateliers' project relative to orthogonality spaces, mereotopology and point-free topology. That could make the unpublished atelier axioms comparable with existing theories.

missed.claim: The definition of figures is explicitly provisional. Grothendieck suggests constraining ρ by the structure of spatial relations but postpones it. The resulting 'spatial atelier' is only 'presumed' to be one on the next page.
missed.quote: On pourrait être plus exigeant ... On ne va pas s'en préoccuper pour le moment.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether At_spat(Σ) satisfies the atelier axioms, and what the right compatibility between ρ and (≤, C) is, is a small open thread in an unpublished framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly definitional. The lattice-theoretic part is classical, and the figure definition is a provisional ingredient of the little-known 'ateliers' project. It is of interest mainly as documentation of that project and its implicit closeness to orthogonality-space and quantum-logic axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: First lines: likely 'Via une telle identification, le rapport d'une partie A de Σ s'identifie à Sup A (= ξ), son orthogonal à Cξ'. 'complément' is probably 'orthogonal'.
In the crossed-out passage, '(𝒜, Δ, |·|)' should read '(A, Δ, |∘|)'. The sentence is 'Ceci dit, à une relation spatiale (A, Δ, |∘|) on associe un spatios (Σ, ≤, C), muni en plus ...'.
'appelle figures du spatios': the image shows 'appelle figure ... spatios' with underlining; possibly 'figure spatiale', consistent with the later 'figures spatiales dans Σ'.
Struck-out 'Figid(Σ)' and 'Figspat(Σ) = {(Φ, ρ) | Φ ∈ (Φ, ρ), ...}' are a first attempt; the definition was rewritten as 'un couple (Φ, ρ), où Φ ⊂ Σ'.
Page header '49' is Grothendieck's numbering; archive page 52.
